weeks.title: Introduction to Corporate Finance and Financial Decision Framework
weeks.description: Explore the purpose of corporate finance, distinguish the four financial decisions and explain how cash flow, time and risk affect company value.
coverage: Purpose and goal of corporate finance
Four recurring decisions: investment, financing, working capital, and distribution
Cash flow, time, risk, stakeholders, and company value
Finance links to HR and management decisions
objectives: Define corporate finance and the role of the financial manager.
Distinguish the four recurring financial decisions.
Explain why cash flow, time, and risk affect value.
Identify financial implications of an HR or management decision.

weeks.title: Financial Statements: Balance Sheet, Income Statement, and Cash Flow Statement
weeks.description: Read the balance sheet, income statement and cash flow statement, explain how they connect and distinguish accounting profit from cash flow.
coverage: Revenue, expenses, profit, and non-cash items
Operating, investing, and financing cash flows
objectives: Identify the main components of the three financial statements.
Explain how the statements connect.
Distinguish accounting profit from cash generated.
Use statement information to answer a short managerial question.

weeks.title: Financial Analysis: Profitability, Liquidity, Efficiency, and Solvency
weeks.description: Calculate and interpret profitability, liquidity, efficiency and solvency ratios to assess financial performance and identify management priorities.
coverage: Leverage, solvency, and limitations of ratio analysis
objectives: Calculate selected financial ratios correctly.
Interpret what each ratio reveals and does not reveal.
Compare performance across time or firms using appropriate caution.
Diagnose a financial strength, weakness, and management priority.

weeks.title: Time Value of Money: Compounding, Present Value, Future Value, and Annuities
weeks.description: Use cash-flow timelines, compounding and discounting to calculate present value, future value and annuities.
objectives: Represent a problem using a cash-flow timeline.
Calculate present and future values.
Calculate the value of a simple annuity.
Explain how rate and time change value.

weeks.title: Risk and Return: Standard Deviation, Beta, CAPM, and Alpha Concept
weeks.description: Calculate expected return and standard deviation, explain diversification and interpret beta, CAPM required returns and alpha.
coverage: CAPM required return and alpha as performance relative to the benchmark
objectives: Calculate and interpret expected return and standard deviation.
Explain diversification and systematic risk.
Interpret beta and estimate a CAPM required return.
Distinguish beta from alpha in clear managerial language.

weeks.title: Investment Decisions: Capital Budgeting and Relevant Cash Flows
weeks.description: Identify incremental project cash flows, exclude sunk costs and account for opportunity costs, working capital and terminal cash flows.
coverage: Sunk costs, opportunity costs, and side effects
Working-capital changes and terminal cash flows
objectives: Identify relevant and irrelevant project cash flows.
Exclude sunk costs and include opportunity costs.
Estimate a simple project cash-flow timeline.
Explain assumptions and cash-flow risks transparently.

weeks.title: Investment Evaluation: NPV, IRR, Payback, Sensitivity, and Scenario Analysis
weeks.description: Evaluate investments using payback, NPV and IRR, then test the recommendation through sensitivity and scenario analysis.
objectives: Calculate payback, NPV, and IRR for a simple project.
Explain the strengths and limitations of each method.
Use NPV as the primary value-creation criterion.
Stress-test a recommendation using sensitivity or scenarios.

weeks.title: Sources of Financing: Internal Funds, Debt, Equity, Bonds, Shares, and IPOs
weeks.description: Compare internal funds, debt and equity, including bonds, shares and IPOs, and weigh their effects on control, flexibility and risk.
coverage: Control, flexibility, maturity, and risk trade-offs
objectives: Distinguish internal, debt, and equity financing.
Compare the advantages and disadvantages of major sources.
Match a financing source to a company's situation.
Explain how financing affects control and risk.

weeks.title: Cost of Capital: Cost of Debt, Cost of Equity, CAPM, and WACC
weeks.description: Estimate the cost of debt and equity, calculate WACC and explain when it is suitable as a discount rate.
objectives: Estimate after-tax cost of debt.
Estimate cost of equity using CAPM.
Calculate WACC using market-value weights.
Explain when WACC is an appropriate discount rate.

weeks.title: Capital Structure: Debt, Equity, Leverage, Financial Risk, and Optimal Mix
weeks.description: Assess debt–equity choices, leverage and financial distress to recommend a capital structure that balances risk and flexibility.
coverage: Capital structure as a managerial trade-off
objectives: Explain how leverage changes return and risk.
Identify benefits and costs of debt financing.
Compare alternative debt-equity mixes.
Recommend a prudent capital structure using evidence and constraints.

weeks.title: Working Capital Management and the Cash Conversion Cycle
weeks.description: Analyse current assets and liabilities, calculate the cash conversion cycle and evaluate ways to improve liquidity.
objectives: Define net working capital and its main components.
Calculate a simple cash conversion cycle.
Explain why growth can create a cash shortage.
Recommend one action to improve liquidity without ignoring operational effects.

weeks.title: Daily Financial Management: Cash, Inventory, Receivables, and EOQ Concept
weeks.description: Evaluate cash, inventory and receivables decisions, including credit policy and the economic order quantity trade-off.
objectives: Identify the costs and benefits of holding cash and inventory.
Evaluate a basic customer credit decision.
Explain the EOQ trade-off and calculate a simple EOQ where required.
Design a balanced daily-finance recommendation.

weeks.title: Profit Distribution: Dividend Policy, Retained Earnings, and Share Repurchases
weeks.description: Compare retained earnings, dividends and share repurchases, considering investment needs, investor expectations and stakeholder effects.
coverage: Growth needs, investor expectations, signalling, and fairness
objectives: Distinguish retained earnings, dividends, and repurchases.
Explain how payout choices interact with investment and financing needs.
Evaluate stakeholder and signalling implications.
Recommend and justify a distribution policy for a case company.

weeks.title: Integrated Case Analysis: Investment, Financing, Operations, and Value Creation
weeks.description: Bring investment, financing and operating decisions together in a company case and defend an evidence-based recommendation.
coverage: Linking cash flow, risk, investment, financing, and liquidity
objectives: Organise a complex case around the four financial decisions.
Select relevant tools instead of calculating everything available.
Identify interactions and trade-offs across decisions.
Present a concise evidence-based recommendation.

weeks.title: Corporate Finance Case Presentation and Summary
weeks.description: Present a financial recommendation, defend assumptions and calculations, and use questions and peer feedback to improve the analysis.
objectives: Communicate financial evidence clearly and professionally.
Defend assumptions and calculations under questioning.
Respond to limitations and alternative interpretations.
Use peer feedback to improve the final recommendation.

weeks.title: Course Review and Exam Preparation
weeks.description: Review key concepts and formulas, practise selecting calculation methods and identify personal priorities for exam preparation.
objectives: Connect the major concepts across the course.
Select the correct method for a stated decision problem.
Complete representative calculations with labelled working.
Diagnose personal errors and prepare an individual review plan.
